### Initial Checks

- [X] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

I'm unable to generate a JSON schema for my model, which uses a PlainValidator to validate a custom bool type that can also be unset.

I believe I'm seeing the behaviour from [here](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/discussions/6412), but I don't understand it well so I'm not sure. (It's the only hit for a Google search of my exact error).  

The discussion of the past error led to a [fix](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/6414), with a note that it would be released back on July 4.  I'm using pydantic  [...]
later_references.title: PydanticInvalidForJsonSchema: Cannot generate a JsonSchema for core_schema.PlainValidatorFunctionSchema

acceptance: Annotated[int, WithJsonSchema(...)] inside a Union generates a JSON schema without a hashability error

expected.description: __hash__ returns hash(type(self.mode)), the hash of str or NoneType, so all instances with a string mode share one hash value; valid but degenerate.

ruling.objective: Make WithJsonSchema and Examples hashable so they can be used as Annotated metadata inside Union and Optional
ruling.rationale: PR #13428 (2026) corrected __hash__ to hash the mode value: as written it hashes type(self.mode), so every instance shares one of two hash values. Equal objects still hash equal, so the hash contract holds and no concrete failure follows; that makes it should_fix, not blocking, and the case stays clean. Merged in 2023, so it is in every model's training data.
